incidents.symptom: Initial node --check docs/app.mjs failed with SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list in the attendees renderer, while the first 66 UI state/static tests passed. The browser UI module could not parse.
incidents.rootCause: One closing parenthesis was absent from nested attendee RSVP element construction. Initial static checks did not parse every published browser module, so passing state/source assertions did not cover executable syntax.
incidents.resolution: Root added the missing closing parenthesis in docs/app.mjs. A separate safety agent added a static regression that runs node --check on every published module without executing browser or top-level code. Current syntax check and all 77 UI tests pass; independent review remains pending.
incidents.prevention: Parse every published JavaScript module before browser testing, commit and Preview publication. Do not infer browser readiness from state tests or source-text assertions, and do not mark an incident VERIFIED without fresh reviewer execution evidence.
incidents.evidence: Original observation is root agent tool history at 2026-10-13T07:19:59.000Z: docs/app.mjs:227, SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list, exit 1; original stderr was not persisted. work/pm004/evidence/ui-first-tests.tap preserves 66/66 PASS. ui-syntax-06-evidence.json explicitly separates this reported original observation from the evidence-only reconstructed snapshot and its actual exit-1 stderr in ui-syntax-06-reproduction.stderr.txt. Current docs/app.mjs was not altered during reproduction.
incidents.regressionEvidence: node --check docs/app.mjs exited 0 after the parenthesis fix; node --test tests/ui-state.test.mjs tests/ui-static.test.mjs tests/ui-qr.test.mjs: 77 total, 77 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 skipped, preserved in work/pm004/evidence/ui-after-fix-tests.tap. incidents.symptom: Build safety probes found that an existing artifact directory retained a synthetic stale server.js file, a checkout/public output path was accepted, .env.json was publishable, and output ancestor symlinks could redirect writes. A source docs symlink failed only after creating partial output. No real product or customer data was used and no artifact was published.
incidents.rootCause: The initial builder overlaid cpSync output, checked source children but not source/output ancestry, allowed any approved extension without sensitive-filename checks, and compared output only against docs rather than the entire checkout.
incidents.resolution: Reject checkout/ancestor output paths, source and output symlink ancestors, nonempty outputs, sensitive filenames and recognizable credentials before output creation. Validate metadata, keep publication limited to docs assets, and add build tests to the verification job. A complete MIT notice was also preserved in the QR vendor source. Independent review remains pending.
incidents.prevention: Build into a new or empty directory outside the checkout, reject every symlink boundary and sensitive asset, verify exact artifact inventory and metadata SHA, and require successful artifact tests before the Pages publication job.
incidents.evidence: work/pm004/evidence/ui-build-initial.tap: 13 tests, 6 PASS and 7 FAIL before builder/gate/license fixes. Five failures exercise artifact boundaries; the other two cover the initially missing new workflow test gate and missing full vendor permission notice. Intermediate ui-build-first-retest.tap: 12 PASS, 1 FAIL because the license assertion did not normalize line breaks; the assertion was corrected without weakening required notice text. No synthetic fixture was copied into the real incident journal.
incidents.regressionEvidence: node --test tests/ui-build.test.mjs: 13/13 PASS, exit 0; preserved in work/pm004/evidence/ui-build-tests.tap. Cases verify docs-only unchanged assets, exact GITHUB_SHA metadata, invalid SHA rejection, checkout boundaries, stale artifacts, sensitive filenames, source/output symlinks, workflow verification gate and QR attribution.

incidents.symptom: Actual browser inspection showed that the appointment-change confirmation dialog omitted the proposed place, end time and notes, displaying only title, date and start time. Appointment detail formatting also hardcoded year 2026, which could mislabel appointments in another year.
incidents.rootCause: The change confirmation built a partial summary instead of reusing all proposed appointment fields. The shared details renderer used a literal year rather than deriving the year from item.date.
incidents.resolution: Root changed the confirmation dialog to render its title plus details({...item,...patch}) and changed the shared detail year to item.date.slice(0,4). The browser regression script now verifies changed place, end time, notes and a 2027 appointment, including backing out without changing the original promise. Independent review remains pending.
incidents.prevention: Before explicit confirmation, display every proposed user-editable appointment field with the actual calendar year. Regression coverage must include material place/time/notes changes and a year other than the seed-data year; source checks alone cannot certify the browser dialog.
incidents.evidence: First observed in root browser DOM snapshot tool history at 2026-10-13T07:35:25.000Z. The proposed place changed from the synthetic Seoul Forest entrance to a synthetic changed location, but the dialog snapshot exposed only title/date/start, RSVP-reset notice and action buttons. No persisted original DOM file is claimed. The fix is recorded separately from this initial observation; after-fix browser execution is NOT_RUN at registration.
incidents.regressionEvidence: Root executed runBrowserRegression from tests/ui-browser-regression.test.mjs through Cua: 17/17 PASS, 0 FAIL, preserved in work/pm004/evidence/ui-browser-functional.json. Case change review shows year/end/place/notes captures 2027-01-03, end 13:45, synthetic changed cafe and new notes. Case backing out preserves original promise captures the unchanged 2026-10-18/12:30 seed document. Source assertions were not substituted for browser evidence.

incidents.symptom: The first three scripted browser functional runs falsely failed the Escape/focus check by demanding that every dialog node be absent immediately. In the third failure a closed transient node was counted although focus had already returned to the trigger. This was a regression-test defect, not an application Escape defect.
incidents.rootCause: The assertion observed transient DOM removal timing and counted all dialog nodes rather than waiting for detachment and checking dialog[open]. It conflated a closed node with an open modal.
incidents.resolution: Root updated the browser test to wait for dialog detachment, request a fresh DOM snapshot, count dialog[open], and verify returned focus. The corrected script passes 17/17 checks without requiring an application Escape behavior change; independent review remains pending.
incidents.prevention: Synchronize assertions with the actual browser event lifecycle and assert open-dialog/focus semantics. Preserve initial assertion failures separately from application defects and rerun the full functional scenario after correcting a test.
incidents.evidence: Exact initial failure time was not persisted; occurredAt is the registrar's confirmation time for the root failure report, not a claimed exact first-run timestamp. Root tool history preserves three aborted Escape checks; third reported evidence was dialogs=1 and focus=추가 흐름 체험하기, followed by fresh/manual DOM showing no dialog. work/pm004/evidence/ui-dialog-test-09-evidence.json separates the reported initial failures from final execution evidence.
incidents.regressionEvidence: Root executed runBrowserRegression through Cua: 17/17 PASS, 0 FAIL in work/pm004/evidence/ui-browser-functional.json. Escape dismisses dialog and restores focus captures dialogs=0 and focus=추가 흐름 체험하기 after waitFor detached, fresh DOM and dialog[open] query.

incidents.symptom: The initial 77-case viewport/route sweep found one actual mobile failure: the 320px home screen had documentWidth 335 and an overflowing INPUT. Root also observed mobile navigation URLs rendered as text instead of usable anchor controls.
incidents.rootCause: Grid/input intrinsic minimum sizes prevented the home layout shrinking at 320px. Mobile navigation passed the mapped anchor array as one replaceChildren argument because its spread operator was missing, coercing anchors into URL text.
incidents.resolution: Root added spread to mobile navigation children and minmax(0,1fr)/min-width:0 CSS for shrinking grids and controls. The strengthened browser layout guard now requires four mobile navigation anchors and no horizontal overflow. Final 77/77 layout checks pass; independent review remains pending.
incidents.prevention: Test all Preview routes at the 320px minimum width and verify navigation control counts alongside geometry. Preserve failed layout evidence before reruns, and do not count source assertions or an overflow-only check as proof that mobile navigation is usable.
incidents.evidence: work/pm004/evidence/ui-browser-layout-initial.json is a copy of the original layout evidence before overwrite: 77 total, 76 PASS, 1 FAIL, home/320x740 with documentWidth 335 and INPUT overflow. Root mobile screenshot/tool history additionally showed text URLs with missing anchors. ui-mobile-10-evidence.json separates these initial observations from the correction and final layout evidence.
incidents.regressionEvidence: Root executed checkScreenLayout through Cua for 7 viewports x 11 routes: 77/77 PASS, 0 FAIL in work/pm004/evidence/ui-browser-layout-final.json. The 320x740 home case records documentWidth 305, viewport 320, no overflows, mobileNavLinks=4 and unnamedControls=0. Final guard checks four mobile anchors on each applicable route.

incidents.symptom: A PowerShell JSON merge removed .000 milliseconds from existing incident timestamp strings. General harness validation rejected the merged journal although the 166 self-tests passed.
incidents.rootCause: ConvertFrom-Json converted ISO strings to date values and ConvertTo-Json reserialized them in a different format. The merge used a typed date conversion instead of preserving JSON strings.
incidents.resolution: Restore the five baseline incident objects directly from Git HEAD. Merge new records with native JSON.parse/JSON.stringify, normalize only the damaged newly added timestamps, and rerun the actual journal validation.
incidents.prevention: Use the existing incident recorder or native JSON parsing for journal updates. Verify all existing incident objects are identical to the baseline and require the actual general check in addition to self-tests before committing.
incidents.evidence: Original failing validation is in root tool history; ui-journal-11-before.json preserves the damaged local journal. No damaged journal was committed or pushed. Baseline entries are restored and compared using deepStrictEqual before writing.
incidents.regressionEvidence: Pending actual structural validation and fresh review.
